transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… I guess what finally scared me enough to come in is, after I eat too much, I’ve been going to the bathroom and making myself throw up so I don’t gain weight. I know that sounds awful. I kept telling myself it was just a one-time thing, like people do foolish things when they’re upset, you know—my sister used to say I worry too much about things like that—but it’s not just once anymore. It’s happened enough that I got frightened.
How often have you found yourself making yourself vomit after eating too much? Has this been happening regularly, like several times a week?

Yes… I mean, I hate saying “regularly,” because it makes it sound so… planned, or like I’m not trying to stop. But for the past several months, most weeks there’s been at least one of those times where I eat in secret, too much, and then I go and make myself sick afterward.

It’s not every day, and some weeks I’ll tell myself I’m doing better, but… no, I can’t honestly call it occasional anymore.
Do you find that your feelings about your body weight or shape have a strong influence on how you feel about yourself overall?

Yes… yes, it really does. I wish it didn’t at my age, you know, I feel silly even saying that. But if I’m getting dressed for church and my skirt feels tight, it can just… spoil the whole morning. Or I’ll be at work and catch myself from the side in one of those store mirrors, and then I can’t stop thinking everyone can see I’ve let myself go.

I’ll try to tell myself people are busy shopping, they’re not studying me, but it still gets in my head and kind of ruins the day.
Do you feel a strong fear of gaining weight or becoming fat, even when you're not overeating?

Yes… I do worry about it, even when I haven’t eaten too much. It’s like it’s always sitting there in the back of my mind.

Like, if I’m getting ready for church and my skirt feels tight, that can just ruin the whole day before I’ve even left the house. Or at work, if I catch myself sideways in one of those store mirrors—those awful mirrors, they’re everywhere—I start thinking, “Everyone can see it. Everyone can tell I’ve let myself go.” I know people are probably just buying socks or looking for a blouse, but I can’t seem to stop thinking about it.
Besides making yourself vomit, have you done anything else to try to keep from gaining weight—like skipping meals, exercising a lot more than you used to, or using laxatives or diet pills?

I… I don’t really know how to answer that neatly. I don’t take anything, not like pills or… well, I don’t think so. I mean, I’ll sometimes tell myself I should “be good” the next day, but then the whole day gets away from me at the store, and customers are asking where the bath towels are, and I’m thinking about what I packed for lunch instead of just doing my job.

As far as laxatives or diet pills, no… not really. Exercise, no, I’m on my feet a lot at work, but that’s not exactly exercise, it’s just walking around folding things and putting things back where they don’t belong. Meals… I might put one off, but I don’t know if I’d call it skipping on purpose. I get a little mixed up with it, honestly.

Can you describe what happens when you eat too much? Do you feel like you're losing control over how much you eat during those times, or is it more about eating in secret and feeling guilty afterward?

It’s… it’s more that once I start, I don’t feel like I’m making proper choices anymore. Like I’ll tell myself, “Just stop now, put it away before he notices,” and then I’m still standing there reaching for one more thing.

And it sounds so foolish when I say it out loud. I can run a till at work and keep track of coupons and returns and all that nonsense, but in that moment it’s like I’m on automatic. I’m thinking I should stop, I really am, but my hand just keeps going.

Can you describe what happens when you feel like you're not making proper choices while eating—like how much you end up eating compared to what you intended, or if you feel like you're eating much more rapidly than usual?

Yes… I suppose it is much more than I mean to. It starts like I’m just going to have a little something when I get home—especially after bridge night, or if I’ve worked late and I’m tired and the store’s been busy, you know, people asking if we have things in the back when we never do.

But then I might have some leftover casserole, and then cookies I baked—because I still bake sometimes, it’s silly, my mother always had something in a tin—and then crackers, and then ice cream. All in one sitting. Not like a normal plate I’d serve myself if anyone was there. I’d never put all that out in front of somebody. It’s more like I keep going back, and before I really let myself think about it, it’s a lot.
Have these eating episodes and the way you feel about your body been causing you a lot of distress, or affecting your daily life—like your work, relationships, or how you take care of yourself?

It does, yes… though I’m still doing the things I’m supposed to do. I go to work, I go to church, I still go to bridge, and from the outside I probably look normal enough. I’m not staying in bed or anything like that.

But I notice I’m planning things around food more than I want to admit. Like if there’s going to be cake after church, I’m already thinking about how to avoid it, or if I can get out quickly. Or with bridge, instead of just enjoying everyone talking and complaining about their husbands and who trumped what, I’m thinking about what’s on the table, and whether I’ll be home alone afterward.

So… yes, it’s making things tense. I still show up, but I don’t feel relaxed in those places the way I used to.

Would you say that during these episodes, you're eating an amount of food that's definitely more than most people would eat in the same amount of time, like in one sitting after work or late at night?

Yes… I think so. I mean, I don’t like thinking of it that way, but if someone else were sitting there, they wouldn’t eat that much.

After bridge, for instance—I’ll come home and maybe have leftover casserole, and then I’ll think, well, just one cookie, since I baked them, and my mother always said you shouldn’t let good food go stale… but then it’s crackers too, and ice cream after that. All in the same sitting.

I’d never put all of that on a plate in front of anybody. It would look ridiculous. But when I’m alone, it sort of happens in pieces, and by the end it’s much more than a person would normally have.
During these times when you're eating more than you mean to, do you feel like you're unable to stop yourself, even if you want to?

Yes… that’s the frightening part, I suppose. Once I start, it’s like I’m on automatic. I’ll be thinking, now stop, that’s enough, your husband will notice if the tin is half-empty or if the ice cream’s gone down too much—though he isn’t always paying attention, men can miss what’s right in front of them, honestly.

But even while I’m thinking that, my hand is still reaching for one more thing. One more cookie, or a bit more of whatever’s there. It doesn’t feel like I’m choosing it the normal way. It feels like I’ve already started and I can’t quite get myself to stop.
During these episodes where you eat more than you intend to, would you say you feel a complete loss of control, like you can't stop eating no matter how hard you try?

Yes… I suppose that’s the honest answer. Once it starts, it feels like I’m on automatic. I can be standing there thinking, stop now, put it away before your husband notices, because he’ll notice if the box is too empty—well, maybe he won’t, he can miss the most obvious things, like the milk sitting right in front of him in the fridge.

But even while I’m thinking all that, I’m still reaching for one more. It doesn’t feel like I can just decide to stop the way I should.
Do you usually eat this way in secret because you're embarrassed or ashamed, or would you feel comfortable doing this in front of others?

I… I’m not sure how to answer that exactly. I don’t think I’d lay it all out in front of someone, if that’s what you mean. I mean, people have snacks with company, don’t they? At bridge someone brings those little cheese straws, and everyone says they’re only having one, and then somehow the plate’s empty before the score cards are even sorted.

But at home… I suppose I don’t really think of it as “in secret” at the time. I’m just in the kitchen, or in the den, and nobody’s around. I wouldn’t want someone standing there watching me, no. That would feel… awful, probably. But I don’t know if that means I’m hiding it exactly. Maybe I am. I don’t know.
On average, how many times per week do these episodes where you feel out of control while eating happen?

Most weeks, I’d say. I hate saying that, because it makes it sound so… regular, like a Tuesday errand or something. But for the past several months it’s been happening most weeks, one of those times where I eat by myself and then end up making myself sick afterward.

I can’t really call it “just now and then” anymore, not honestly.
